pairs.subject: readiness-passports
pairs.evidence: src/app/api/report/passport/overrides/route.ts:137 The server write door validates decline paths against the allow-list but never rejects a missing or empty reason. parseDeclined just drops a blank reason, and route.test.ts:160 sends `{}` and gets past validation to the 404 stage. So the 'reason is required' rule exists only in the PassportDeclineControl UI, and any other client can file a decline with no rationale.

techniques.evidence: src/app/api/report/passport/overrides/route.ts:137 Several parts conform: an allow-list checked at the door (route.ts:123-124, isDeclinablePath over the literal DECLINABLE_PATHS), an overlay stored beside the scan, and `by`/`at` stamped by the server (lines 133-149). But the technique says the reason is required and rejected if empty, at one validation door. Here that rule lives only in the client control (PassportDeclineControl.tsx:14), so the door accepts a decline without a reason.

src/app/api/report/passport/pr/route.ts:60 The portable artifact committed to the customer repo carries a schema version and pointer. It also carries a generatedAt day and an unversioned generatedBy "ascent-scan" (passport.ts:543-546). It does NOT carry the immutable commit SHA it observed, which the AppPassport header in types.ts:383-390 has no field for; the SHA is only a lookup key beside the row (route.ts:40 headSha). It also has no assessor or ladder version. Migrate-on-read is realized (route.ts:55 upgradePassport, tagged migratedFrom).
src/app/api/report/passport/pr/route.ts:79 The PR body reports the two axes as a pair (automation level, production band) with no averaged headline across them.

src/app/api/report/passport/route.ts:3 The served artifact is deliberately tool-naming. Its monitoring and hosting fields are three-valued (vendor name / null meaning looked-and-none / "unknown"), per types.ts:414-419.
